title: Bumpus to Meany: 15 May or 15 June 1907?
text: The PI's terse timeline dates Bumpus's reassurance to Meany 15 May 1907; the transcription file and comprehensive timeline date the same letter 15 June 1907. The letter says Bumpus 'Has returned from abroad to find Meany's May 12 letter unanswered'; the Assistant Secretary wrote on 6 May that Bumpus had 'rather unexpectedly sailed for Europe last Wednesday' and was expected back 'the end of the month'. The two PI documents disagree; the record is shown with the transcription's date and this note.

title: Reed to Startsman: 18 October or 26 October 1906?
text: The PI header for the copy reads 18 October 1906; the archive's index entry quoted with Stone's letter lists 'Oct 26, 06, Reed to Startsman'. Not resolved.

title: Departure from New York, 1908: 19 May or 'toward the end of May'?
text: LSQ's letter of 19 May 1908 ('I leave this evening'), his report ('a week earlier than the date first agreed upon (May 27th)') and Sherwood's 1909 letter ('he left New York on May 19, 1908') give 19 May. The PI's timeline entry from the Bulletin (B.AMNH 26, p.90) reads '"toward the end of May" 1908'. The Bulletin text was not provided to check the quotation.

title: Seward Peninsula crossing: 4½ days from Nome, or 4–5 days from Lane's Landing?
text: LSQ's report: 'The crossing from Nome to Candle occupied four and one half days'. His letter from Lane's Landing (24 June 1908) says he hopes to be at Candle 'in four or five days'. If he reached Nome on 21 June and was already at the railhead on 24 June, the two statements cannot both be exact.

title: How far up the Buckland? 86 ('estimated') or 'about 80' miles
text: LSQ: 'a point estimated at 86 miles above the mouth'. The Tale: 'turned back about 80 miles inland'. Both are estimates; the river was not surveyed by LSQ.

title: 'Five days' in Nome between 4 and 13 August 1907
text: The PI's summary of B.AMNH 26, p.89 has LSQ arriving at Nome 4 August, staying 'five days' and leaving on the Corwin 13 August. The interval is nine days; the Solomon River trip may account for part of it, but the Bulletin's wording was not available.

title: Railhead: 'Lane's Landing' (LSQ) vs 'Shelton' (Bulletin via PI)
text: Two names for the head of the Seward Peninsula Railroad occur in two provided sources. GNIS records 'Shelton (historical)' but has no entry for Lane's Landing. Whether the names denote one place is not stated in the provided material.

title: 'Hotham Peninsula' has no modern gazetteer entry
text: LSQ crossed 'Hotham Peninsula' on foot between Eschscholtz Bay and Hotham Inlet. GNIS names that land Baldwin Peninsula. The identification is the model's inference from the described route and is marked 'inferred'.

title: Keewalik / Kiwalik; 'the spit'
text: All provided sources spell the outfitting point 'Keewalik'; GNIS spells it 'Kiwalik'. The Bulletin (via PI) also calls it 'the spit'. The spelling equivalence is a model identification.

title: Name variants across the file
text: Meany/Meaney; Startsman/Startson/Statesman; E.W. Graham/'C.W. Graham [sic]'; Matthew/Matthews (W.D. Matthew) and J.F. Matthews/Mathews (1914, a different person); Eschscholtz/Eschholz/Exchscholtz; Rainier Grand/Ranier Grande/Rainer Grand Hotel; Mastodon/Mammoth (the A-Y-P parties and Bumpus's early letters say 'mastodon', the Museum's scientists 'mammoth'; Bumpus's 1907 draft instructions strike 'Mastodon' for 'Mammoth' in pencil).

title: Where was Grant's / Stone's camp?
text: Osborn (20 June 1907): Eschscholtz Bay—'big bone beach'—'is only 30 miles from Stone's camp'. Bumpus's pencilled instructions (29 June 1907): 'Mr. Grants camp on big bone beach'. The Tale: Grant 'was headed to his ranch near Nome'. Three placements; none can be fixed.

title: Did Quackenbush travel with Grant from New York?
text: Bumpus to Jesup (28 June 1907) planned that LSQ 'will leave for Alaska with Mr. Grant on July 2'; Grant (3 July) was 'delighted to have him with me'; the Bulletin (via PI) has LSQ leaving New York on 5 July; the Tale says LSQ 'left for Alaska in the company of Madison Grant'. The Bulletin itinerary separates them at Fort Gibbon (Grant to Fairbanks) and has Grant 'part ways' at Nome. Grant's own itinerary is otherwise undocumented in the file.

title: Tale: Chambers's Edinburgh Journal dated 1855 in text, 1852 in footnote
text: An internal inconsistency in the PI's talk text, recorded as found.

title: What was found: the Tale's two inventories
text: The Tale's introduction: 'All Quackenbush found were a hip bone and femur, some skull fragments and vertebrae, and a tail still encased in skin and fur'. Its §3, following the Bulletin: hip and leg bones, lower jaw with teeth, two tusks, skull fragments, vertebrae, the tail, 'a small quantity of flesh, skin, hair and wool'. LSQ's 1908 report adds ribs, foot bones, and 'a piece of skin three feet long, found under the innominate bone'. The fuller lists supersede the summary.

title: Paying for 1908: 'Total expense 1908 was $1,712.27' against a share of $856.14
text: Sherwood to Pyne (15 January 1909, PI summary): 'Total expense 1908 was $1,712.27'. Sherwood to Morgan (21 January): a check 'for share, $856.14'; Morgan replies that he bears 'one-half of the cost'; Pyne 'accords with Morgan's proposal'. Two shares of $856.14 would come to $1,712.28, one cent more than the stated total. The file does not say how the halves were computed; the figures are kept as written and no total is computed in the funding view.

title: The PI's timeline writes 'LSQ writes from Shelton' for the letter headed Lane's Landing
text: Quackenbush's letter of 24 June 1908 is headed Lane's Landing; the PI's terse timeline entry for the same letter reads 'LSQ writes from Shelton'. One provided source therefore treats the two names as one place, while the letter and the Bulletin (via the PI) use different names. The equation is the PI's reading and is recorded as such; the place record keeps both attested names.

title: Grant, 1930: 'the only mammoth ever found in the flesh in the Eastern Hemisphere'
text: Grant's form slip to Osborn (7 June 1930) says of the Alaska find, 'This is the only mammoth ever found in the flesh in the Eastern Hemisphere.' The whole file places the find in Alaska; the slip's hemisphere stands against it. The wording is recorded as written and is not corrected.

title: 'Mr. Schubert[?] of the U.S. National Yale Museum' — 'U.S. National' struck
text: Osborn's draft terms (16 April 1907) name as a possible arbiter 'Mr. Schubert[?] of the U.S. National Yale Museum'; in the transcription 'U.S. National' is struck through, leaving the Yale Museum, and the name carries the PI's query mark. The record p_schubert follows the unstruck text (Yale) and keeps the full wording here.

title: Removal slip: 'Taken by for Mr. Quackenbush', as written
text: The removal slip of 28 April 1908 reads 'Taken by for Mr. Quackenbush'. Whether 'by' is a slip of the pen or marks a name left blank is not stated; the wording is kept as transcribed and not emended.

title: Osborn to Bumpus, 20 June 1907, filed under 'Alaska Mammoth Exp. 1906'
text: The PI records the location of Osborn's letter of 20 June 1907 as Central Archives 590, Box 162, Folder 'Alaska Mammoth Exp. 1906', although the letter belongs to the 1907 expedition. Whether this is the archive's filing or a slip in the PI's note is not stated; the citation is kept as recorded.

title: 'Robert T. Varnum, Secretary.' — struck through on the Taylor Creek Ditch Co. letterhead
text: The letterhead of Stone to Bumpus (20 June 1907) lists the company's officers; the last line, 'Robert T. Varnum, Secretary.', is struck through in the transcription. The struck name is recorded in the prosopography; no office is asserted and no tie to the other officers is drawn. Letterhead officer lists are printed, not written by the signer, and ties resting on them are tagged 'letterhead' in the network.

title: Osborn to Bumpus, 20 June 1907: first page not fully photographed
text: The PI notes 'don't have full photo of first page of letter' and reconstructs it from the archive index entry and legible fragments. The passage in which Osborn announced Anderson's withdrawal and Grant's departure is therefore known only in summary.

title: Osborn to Bumpus, 16 April 1907: a marginal note cut off in the photograph
text: '[A note in left hand margin that my photo cut off]' (PI).

title: A letter to Quackenbush dated 2 July [1907] was removed from the file on 28 April 1908 and not returned
text: The removal slip reads 'Correspondent:_________ to “Quackenbush. Date of Letter: July 2. Taken by for Mr. Quackenbush. Date Apr 28 ’08 Returned:___________.' — as written (see f_removal_slip_wording). 28 April 1908 is the date of LSQ's 1908 commission. The letter's content and author are unknown.

title: Bumpus to Grant, 1 July 1907: enclosure (copy of LSQ's instructions) not in file
text: 'NB no enclosure' (PI).

title: LSQ's paper and 'the letter from Mr. Granger' (March 1908) not in file
text: Osborn asked Bumpus to judge 'whether we desire to publish at this length?'. 'Neither included in file' (PI). The paper survives separately as the 15-page manuscript in the Osborn Papers, untranscribed.

title: 'A Mammoth Hunt in Alaska, in 1907' (15 pp. ms) — exists, not transcribed, not provided
text: PI note: '**need to read, take notes. RJHW 5/9/2019.' Osborn's annotation: 'not to be used for Bulletin'.

title: The Bulletin article (B.AMNH 26) itself was not provided
text: All itinerary dates marked 'via PI' rest on the PI's reading of pages 88–91; quotations from pp. 89–90, 107, 110 and 125 are known only through the Tale and timelines.

title: Letters referred to but not in the file
text: Osborn's letter to LSQ about the change of plans (Bumpus, 30 Apr 1907: 'has already written to you'); Osborn's letter to LSQ of February 1908 (memorandum); Hoffman's letter asking to go again (LSQ, 27 Mar 1908); J.F. Matthews's letter from Alaska (1914, returned to Grant); Lucas's intended letter to Matthews; Osborn's letter to Morgan ('H.F.O. has written', undated note); any reply from Startsman or Graham to the Museum; the telegrams LSQ was instructed to send 'by wire'.

title: Conversations and calls that never entered the file
text: Chilberg's 'conference' with Startsman at Nome (1906); the A-Y-P Executive Committee meeting that found the expense 'too great'; Bumpus's and Osborn's 'conference with Mr. Quackenbush' (June 1907); Grant's call on Osborn explaining his Alaska plans; Grant's and LSQ's visit to the Museum (February 1908); Bumpus's suggestion that Osborn 'call up Pyne long distance'; Grant's 1914 attempt to reach Osborn 'on the 'phone'; whatever LSQ 'told' Grant of the 1908 trip that made the written report seem 'barren'.

title: People who are never named
text: The 'old Indian' who found the reported mammoth (d. 1900); Jim Hoffman, who is 'a man' or 'the man who was with me' in every Quackenbush letter and is named only in the Bulletin (via PI) and the Tale; the 'engineer and man' Startsman proposed to hire; the men at the two settlements of the 1908 crossing ('two stops were made at settlements'); 'the Eskimos' from whom specimens might be bought; the 'prospectors' who vouched for the Buckland; the signers of the Assistant Secretary's, Assistant Treasurer's and Secretary's copies; the author of the February 1908 memorandum and of the 25 February 1908 letter to Osborn.

title: The reported mammoth's location was never disclosed
text: Reed anticipated that Startsman 'would not want to disclose the place'; Matthew proposed a bond 'not to reveal the locality'; Bumpus's only hint is 'some two hundred miles up the Yukon River from Nome'. Quackenbush was never shown the body. No point is drawn.

title: Coffee Creek (1914): six candidates in GNIS, none chosen
text: Grant 'know[s] the location' but does not write it down.

title: 'The map' Quackenbush took on 5 July 1907 is unidentified
text: LSQ: 'I took the other copies which you made for me and the map.' In 1909 the Museum sought the 1906 Post Route Map of Alaska; whether this was the same map is not stated. No historical map was available for the geocoding tier 3.

title: Folder titles unknown for the 1910, 1914 and 1916 items
text: The PI records 'Folder: [???]' for Central Archives 262 (Box 92), 4 (Box 4) and 51 (Box 22).

title: How did the Reed/Startsman copies reach the AMNH file?
text: The three copies (Reed to Startsman; Startsman and Graham to Reed; Reed to Chilberg) sit in the '1906' folder. Meany enclosed 'some letters' on 18 March 1907; the index to Stone's letter of 20 June 1907 also records 'Attached copies Feb. 26 Reed to Chilberg, Oct 26, 06, Reed to Startsman, Dec. 30, S. to Reed' (via Anderson). Two possible transmissions; the transcription does not say which copies are which.

title: Two PI files, four word-level variants
text: The transcription file (LS_Quackenbush.docx) and the comprehensive timeline (Mammoth_Expeditions_TIMELINE.docx) carry the same transcriptions with four differences in the 1907 instructions and the Rathbun letter: 'per month' / 'per moth'; 'can be made' / 'can by made'; 'well-acquainted' / 'well-acquantied'; 'urded' / 'urged'. This site follows the transcription file and records the variants here.

title: Tale footnote 46 is a list of author names only
text: 'Werrit, Asiminogov, Koroloff, Gordin, Schultz.' — the PI's shorthand for literature on the St Petersburg Academy; no titles given.

title: Whose prose is on this site
text: Verbatim blocks: the historical writers, as transcribed by the PI (Rebecca J. H. Woods), with her [sic], [?], [illeg] and colour marks preserved. Summary blocks: the PI's paraphrases. Editorial blocks: the PI's descriptions of the physical documents and her dated research notes. Story backbone: the PI's talk text (2019), quoted verbatim. Gazetteer coordinates: USGS GNIS, CGNDB, GeoNames, with Wikidata cross-checks. Everything else on the site — the selection and ordering of quotations, the typing of blocks, the geocoding decisions, the network rules, the connective labels — is the model's work and is labelled 'model'.
